source_paper_text:
Unsplittable Transshipments
Srinwanti Debgupta, Sarah Morell, and Martin Skutella
53rd International Colloquium on Automata, Languages, and Programming (ICALP 2026)

We study unsplittable transshipments as an extension of single source unsplittable flows
to networks with multiple sources and sinks and prescribed supplies and demands, where
for each source–sink pair flow is routed along at most one path. More precisely, we are
given a directed graph D = (V, A) together with a vertex balance function b : V → ℝ
satisfying ∑_{v∈V} b(v) = 0. A vertex v is called a source if b(v) > 0, and the set of all
sources is denoted by S⁺. Similarly, a vertex v is called a sink if b(v) < 0, and the set of
all sinks is denoted by S⁻. A flow x ∈ ℝ^A_{≥0} is a b-transshipment if

∑_{a∈δout(v)} x_a − ∑_{a∈δin(v)} x_a = b(v) for all v ∈ V,

where δin(v) and δout(v) denote the sets of incoming and outgoing arcs of vertex v,
respectively. An unsplittable b-transshipment is a b-transshipment together with a path
decomposition consisting of source–sink paths only, and with at most one path for each
source–sink pair. In order to emphasize the fact that a particular transshipment x is not
necessarily unsplittable, we sometimes refer to x as a fractional transshipment.

The rich literature on SSUF mostly refers to the demand values at sinks as d_t := |b(t)|
for t ∈ S⁻. Here d_max := max_{t∈S⁻} d_t denotes the maximum demand of any sink.

In this section, we modify the DGG Algorithm and its analysis in order to compute
unsplittable transshipments with bounded congestion. We are given an acyclic digraph
D = (V, A) with a set of sources S⁺ and a set of sinks S⁻, together with supplies and
demands specified by a balance function b : V → ℝ and a fractional b-transshipment x.

The Modified DGG Algorithm can be adapted to guarantee lower bounds on arc flows in
unsplittable transshipments; see Theorem 6. Whether arc-wise upper and lower bounds can
be achieved simultaneously remains an intriguing open question, even in the special SSUF
case. Extending a conjecture for SSUF by Morell and Skutella [13], we conjecture that such
transshipments exist and can be computed efficiently.

Conjecture 12. Given a b-transshipment x, one can efficiently compute an unsplittable
b-transshipment y such that

x_a − d_max ≤ y_a ≤ x_a + d_max for all a ∈ A.
target: For every finite acyclic digraph D=(V,A), nonzero rational balance function b:V->Q with sum_v b(v)=0, and nonnegative rational b-transshipment x satisfying sum_{a out of v} x_a - sum_{a into v} x_a = b(v) for every v, compute in polynomial time a nonnegative b-transshipment y admitting a weighted decomposition into directed source-to-sink paths with at most one positive-weight path for each ordered source-sink pair, such that x_a-d_max <= y_a <= x_a+d_max for every arc a, where sources have b>0, sinks have b<0, and d_max=max_{t:b(t)<0}|b(t)|. This rational-input statement is a bit-model operationalization narrower than the source's literal real-valued domain; prove or rigorously disprove this exact operationalized claim.
title: Two-sided arc bounds for unsplittable transshipments
